newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Telekom sell-off to begin in 1997 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Turk Telekom sell-off to begin in 1997 2nd half.

text.p: The first tranche of Turkey's state telecommunications company Turk Telekom will be privatised in the second half of 1997, the head of the country's privatisation administration (OIB) said on Wednesday.

These two privatisations are key to the government's aim of speeding up sell-offs this year as a way of raising badly needed revenues. The government is aiming to raise $5 billion from privatisations this year.
Karakaya said revenues of $500 million were expected in January, when the sale of Etibank, split into three banks, is to be completed.
Karakaya said a consensus had been reached by government ministries on the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) for fuel oil, which would become effective after the legal process has been completed.
This mechanism would allow the privatisation of state refiner Tupras, he said.
The APM envisages abolishing government subsidies and setting up parameters which take into account crude prices, freight prices and FOB sale prices of petroleum products in Italy.
Turkey's only private refinery Atas, largely owned by Mobil and British Petroleum stopped production last October over losses due to subsidised pricing.
The Turkish arm of Mobil said in December that operations would resume after the new formula had been put into practice.
Karakaya said large foreign interest was expected in the planned sell-offs.
"About 20 percent, or $626 million, of privatisation revenues of $3.1 billion in the past 10 years have come from foreign investors," he said.
"Therefore 1997 will be a key year in terms of foreign capital influx to Turkey. Otherwise, with local capital such privatisation plans cannot easily be realised," he said.
He also said work to prepare some power plants for privatisation was under way and would be completed soon.
